v1.feedback: The rubato concept maps well — tempo-stealing modulated into differential-growth density variation along the polyline, with asymmetric lingering (dense coral zones) vs rushing (vertical leaps). No banned techniques; palette inherits the parent's ash→rust→bone earth tones. Two concerns: (1) the rubato breathing may be too subtle to read in 2 seconds — RUBATO_DEPTH at 0.72 sounds aggressive on paper but the visual gap between 'dense knotted zone' and 'stretched gap' needs to be unmistakable in the silhouette, consider widening MAX_D threshold divergence between lingering and rushing zones so the density contrast is architectural rather than textural; (2) the vertex `rubato` value is stored but the visible shader section is identical to the parent — if the truncated portion doesn't modulate point size or color warmth by rubato factor, the piece will look indistinguishable from 2m2 at a glance, which undercuts the chain requirement. Make the rubato zones visually legible: warmer/larger points in lingering zones, cooler/smaller in rushing zones.
